title: Add validation gates: GPU health + driver/CUDA parity (pre/post provisioning)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
links: GitHub: redwood/pr-18429 (record validation artifacts + failure reasons)
GitHub: redwood/pr-18452 (quarantine on repeat validation failures)
description:
Context
- Part of the Provision-to-ready automation sprint. We need automated validation gates that are authoritative enough to block nodes from joining serving pools, but actionable for on-call.
- This ticket covers two of the highest-signal gates:
  1) GPU health checks (hardware + driver stack sanity)
  2) Driver/CUDA/NCCL parity checks (detect drift from the golden image + avoid mixed stacks within a pool)

Goal
- Prevent unhealthy or misconfigured GPU nodes from ever reaching Ready.
- Catch driver/toolkit drift early (before inference workloads) and provide precise failure reasons.
- Support staged rollout constraints (initially us-east + A100) but design gates to work across GPU types and regions.

Non-goals
- Not implementing the NCCL fabric smoke test here (tracked in ENG-4824).
- Not implementing the global quarantine policy logic (ENG-4825/PR-18452), but our checks must produce structured results compatible with it.

Implementation plan
A) GPU health validation (post-provision, before Ready)
- Run via validation-agent DaemonSet on target nodes.
- Collect and evaluate:
  - `nvidia-smi -L` and `nvidia-smi -q` basic availability (driver responding, expected GPU count).
  - ECC health signals:
    - Fail gate on any "volatile" double-bit ECC errors.
    - Warn (but do not fail) on single-bit ECC errors above threshold unless repeated across reboots.
  - Xid errors:
    - Fail gate if recent Xid codes in the last N minutes are in the "quarantine-worthy" set (initial set: 31/43/45/48/79/109; exact mapping documented in agent config).
    - Ignore known-benign transient codes when explicitly allowlisted.
  - Persistence mode and power management sanity:
    - Validate persistence mode is enabled where required by baseline.
    - Validate no GPU is in a "lost" state.
  - DCGM optional mode (behind feature flag): if dcgm-exporter present, run a quick diagnostic (level 1) and treat failures as gate failures.

B) Driver/CUDA/NCCL parity validation
- The golden image pipeline produces an "expected stack" manifest (driver version, CUDA runtime version, NCCL version) per image channel (candidate/stable).
- Validation-agent reads "expected stack" from control-plane readiness service (by pool_id + image_channel) and compares against node-reported versions.
- What we compare:
  - NVIDIA driver version (from `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader`)
  - CUDA runtime version (from `nvidia-smi` output and/or `nvcc --version` when present)
  - NCCL library version (from `libnccl.so` package metadata; distro-specific fallback)
- Policy:
  - Fail gate if driver version mismatches expected major.minor.patch.
  - Fail gate if CUDA minor differs from expected (we pin CUDA minor during this sprint to reduce flake / mixed stacks).
  - NCCL version: allow patch-level drift if ABI-compatible (config-driven), otherwise fail.
- Output structured failure reason including: expected vs observed + remediation suggestion (reimage vs drain/retry).

C) Mixed GPU SKU edge cases
- Dedicated pools should not intentionally mix GPU SKUs, but we have seen transient states during capacity events and mis-tagged instances.
- Add a guard:
  - Determine SKU from PCI IDs / `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name`.
  - Compare against pool’s expected SKU(s) from provisioning metadata.
  - Fail gate if a node’s detected SKU is not in the pool allowlist.
- For known multi-SKU pools (future), allowlist supports multiple entries, but still emits a warning if the pool contains >1 SKU at once (metric only).

D) Observability + artifacts
- For each gate, emit:
  - Validation step name (e.g., `gpu.health`, `stack.parity`, `gpu.sku_guard`)
  - Start/end timestamps, duration
  - Result (pass/fail) + failure_code (stable enum) + short failure_message
  - Pointer to bundled logs (object storage URL or log index reference)
- Metrics (no per-node IDs):
  - `fleet.validation.pass_count{step,region,gpu_type,pool_type,image_channel}`
  - `fleet.validation.fail_count{step,region,gpu_type,pool_type,image_channel,failure_code}`
  - `fleet.validation.duration_ms{step,region,gpu_type,pool_type,image_channel}`

Acceptance criteria
- When GPU health check fails, node MUST remain in Validating (or transition to Quarantined based on orchestration policy), and must not join serving pools.
- When driver/CUDA parity fails, failure reason must include expected vs observed versions, and recommend reimage.
- Checks must be deterministic and not depend on internet access.
- Produces structured artifacts stored via readiness service; operators can see failure_code and log pointer in tooling.
- Handles the following edge cases:
  1) Mixed GPU SKUs detected in a pool -> fail with `SKU_MISMATCH`.
  2) Driver drift (node on older driver than expected) -> fail with `DRIVER_VERSION_MISMATCH`.
  3) Driver drift (node on newer driver than expected) -> fail with `DRIVER_VERSION_MISMATCH` (prefer fail-closed during sprint).
  4) `nvidia-smi` times out or errors -> fail with `NVIDIA_SMI_UNAVAILABLE`.
  5) GPU count mismatch (expected 8, saw 7) -> fail with `GPU_COUNT_MISMATCH`.
  6) Xid errors present in recent window -> fail with `GPU_XID_RECENT`.

Test plan
- Unit tests (validation agent):
  - Parse fixtures for `nvidia-smi -q` output (healthy/unhealthy, ECC/Xid variants).
  - Version comparison tests (driver/CUDA/NCCL) including allowlisted patch drift.
  - SKU parsing tests for common names (A100 80GB PCIe vs SXM variants as separate SKUs).
- Integration tests (kind-like / staging cluster):
  - Golden image manifest is fetched and compared correctly by pool_id/image_channel.
  - Simulate drift by overriding agent-reported driver version and ensure gate fails + artifact stored.
  - Ensure readiness service records step durations + failure_code.
- Canary / rollout validation:
  - During us-east A100 staged rollout, compare validation failure rate to baseline (<2% expected after initial bake stabilization).

Rollout notes
- Gate enforcement is behind feature flag (region + gpu_type scoped). Start with us-east + A100 only.
- Fail-closed for parity mismatch; we can relax once image pipeline promotion is stable.

Operational guidance (for runbook)
- DRIVER_VERSION_MISMATCH / CUDA_VERSION_MISMATCH: reimage node to pool’s current stable image; if widespread, halt rollout and evaluate image promotion.
- GPU_XID_RECENT: drain and quarantine node; if repeats after reimage, treat as potential hardware issue.
- NVIDIA_SMI_UNAVAILABLE: check driver modules and kubelet/container runtime; often indicates partial driver install or a broken image bake.

Open questions
- Confirm final list of Xid codes to fail vs warn (need Infra + SRE alignment).
- Confirm whether we should allow “newer driver than expected” in emergency capacity scenarios (proposal: keep fail-closed during sprint).

Progress updates
- 2025-10-04: Drafted failure_code enums + initial policy (fail-closed) and shared with SRE for review.
- 2025-10-07: Implemented GPU health parsing + artifacts emission; added SKU guard; sent PR for review.
- 2025-10-10: Added parity comparison against expected stack manifest; aligned naming with readiness service fields.
- 2025-10-14: Addressed review feedback: reduce metric cardinality (removed node_id tags), improved error messages and log bundling.
- 2025-10-18: Staged rollout confirmed in us-east A100. Validation flake rate acceptable; remaining flake work tracked in ENG-4830.
comments: 2025-10-04 (Miles Thornton): Please make failure_code stable and queryable; avoid putting raw driver strings in metric labels. Artifact body/log bundle is fine.
2025-10-06 (Aisha Bello): Ensure metrics are aggregate only; no pool_id in alerts initially. We can add pool_id to dashboards via logs/queries later if needed.
2025-10-07 (Nina Petrova): SKU matching: distinguish A100 PCIe vs SXM; we saw a misprovision that looked like 'A100-SXM4-80GB' when the pool expected PCIe.
2025-10-09 (Keiko Yamamoto): For parity mismatches, fail-closed is correct for sprint. Make sure remediation message says reimage and does not suggest manual driver install.
2025-10-12 (Ethan Park): Ensure readiness service stores expected_stack_version used for evaluation (for forensics when image channel changes).
2025-10-14 (Vanessa Ortiz): +1 on default quarantine after repeated failures; but this ticket should only emit clear reasons and let orchestrator decide transitions.
resolution: Merged validation-agent updates to run GPU health + stack parity gates, store artifacts/failure reasons, and block readiness until pass. Enabled behind staged rollout flag for us-east A100. Follow-ups for flake/timeout tuning tracked in ENG-4830.
